title: The DipEncoder: Enforcing Multimodality in Autoencoders

problem.claim: Improve cluster structure by enforcing multimodality in an autoencoder embedding.

contributions.claim: Applies the Dip-test gradient with respect to both the projection axis and the data.
Tightly couples the Dip-test with an autoencoder to produce an embedding that separates clusters.
Introduces DipEncoder as the basis of a deep clustering algorithm.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe DipEncoder as the basis of a novel deep clustering algorithm.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments show that DipEncoder is highly competitive with state-of-the-art methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Hartigan's Dip-test has gained interest in unsupervised learning and does not require complex parameterization or an assumed distribution.
Dip-values can identify a projection axis associated with multimodal structures.
The method applies the gradient to the projection axis and the data to improve cluster structure.
Coupling the Dip-test with an autoencoder yields an embedding that separates clusters.
Experiments report competitiveness with state-of-the-art methods.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, metrics, and numerical results are not specified.
